title: DWP v6 per-task context manifest
description: The derived, read-only context selection for ONE task of a v6 plan, produced by shared/context_manifest.py (spec/V6_CONTEXT.md): the cheap re-anchoring surface an executing agent loads instead of history. Never hand-edited and never a source of truth - every value is recomputed from the contract and the journal, so two derivations over the same records are identical (deterministic under replay; as_of carries the records' position and timestamp, not a wall clock). Context pruning can never hide the acceptance or authorization boundary: the three mandatory sections (authorization, repository_rules, acceptance) are unconditional, and a --sections request that would drop one is refused.

derived_by.description: The shipped helper identity that produced this derivation; a document produced by any other path must not wear this schema.

plan.description: The plan folder name, mirrored from the contract.

contract_id.description: The live contract's content-addressed identity this derivation was computed against.

contract_revision.description: The live contract's revision; after an amendment this is the highest revision under contracts/.

task.description: The task id this manifest selects context for.

last_seq.description: The journal sequence of the last event included; the manifest is stale by definition once the journal grows past it.

event_ts.description: The timestamp of that last event (the scheduler's clock, A11).

approvals.description: Approval events citing the live contract id - the running authority (task_start is refused without one).

mechanism.description: How authority was granted (plan_authorship or pre_authorization); the mechanism is recorded honestly and both gate identically (A2/A3).

contract_authorization.description: The contract's authorization block verbatim; its shape is governed by plan-contract/v6.json, not restated here.

permissions.description: The contract's permissions block verbatim (granted / not_granted); its shape is governed by plan-contract/v6.json, not restated here.

scope.description: The contract's scope block verbatim (allowed_paths, allowed_command_classes, forbidden_operations); governed by plan-contract/v6.json.

invariants.description: Per declared invariant: the statement, plus the latest grammar-matching observation's state (pass / fail / stale / unevaluated).

seq.description: The seq of the observation that produced the state, or null when unevaluated.

detail.description: The fail/stale detail when the state carries one.

dependencies.description: The contract's dependencies block verbatim (pinned inputs, external systems); governed by plan-contract/v6.json.

files.description: Repo-relative path to its sha256 content digest; a null value means the entry is missing on disk.

widen_discovery.description: True when discovery must widen this cycle: a touched-surface entry is missing on disk, or the surface's impact is unmapped (no in-window accepted evidence yet).

acceptance.description: This task's criteria with their closure decisions, recomputed by outcomes.py closure - a projection, never a declaration.

control_kind.description: none for evidence-closed criteria; regression/discrimination require an executed, in-window, discriminating control pair.

mechanism.description: How it closes or why it is still open: control_pair, evidence, reconciled, or an open/blocked explanation string.

via_seq.description: The journal seq of the closing record when one exists.

verdict.description: The control verdict that closed a controlled criterion.

trust.description: The trust label of the closing evidence; observed means a shipped helper itself executed the check (A1).

evidence_path.description: Pointer to the recorded evidence artifact under the plan.

authority.description: The amendment authority behind a reconciled closure (A4/D2-4).

evidence.description: In-window accepted evidence for this task's satisfied criteria, with pointers that are re-checked against disk at derivation time.

pointer_resolves.description: Whether the evidence artifact exists on disk at derivation time; a dangling pointer is surfaced, never hidden.

step.description: The deterministic ladder's first match, in order: approval -> start -> authority -> control -> evidence -> complete.

action.description: The concrete command or authority act the ladder prescribes.

criteria.description: The criteria the step addresses, when it addresses specific ones.

dead_ends.description: The U4 digest: recorded dead approaches (failed gates, refusals, refused adaptations, non-discriminating controls), retention-biased - an entry leaves only on a proven record fact, never on a mere surface change.

aged_out.description: Why the entry no longer gates discovery (e.g. a superseded contract revision).

inputs_fingerprint.description: Digest over the contract id and the current touched-surface digests; a stored fingerprint different from the current one invalidates the summary that carries it.

rule.description: The freshness rule in words, restated with every derivation.

history_triggers.description: Optional section: the ONLY declared triggers under which history beyond this manifest loads (none, a handoff, an amendment affecting this task).
